title: Institutional volume drives market direction
claim: 90 percent or more of trading volume in large markets is institutional; therefore market movement must reflect institutional intent and entry/exit decisions
support: Brooks states that since institutions dominate volume and are consistently profitable, all retail trades occur with an institution taking the opposite side. Algorithmic dominance has increased significantly since 2011; exact percentages and behavior may be outdated.
mechanism: Market participants are predominantly algorithmic/institutional systems; retail traders must align with their directional bias
assumptions: Institutional volume data stable over analysis period
failure_modes: Algorithm changes by major market participants
Shift in market structure (e.g., retail consolidation)
validation: Can cross-reference with market structure data from SEC/exchanges

title: Algorithmic trading creates more precise support/resistance
claim: As algorithmic trading increases, support/resistance levels should become more sharply defined and measured move projections more precise due to mathematical logic replacing emotion
support: Brooks infers that computer programs using objective mathematical analysis would tend toward support/resistance precision and tighter channels. Analysis from 2011; algorithmic landscape radically changed since then.
mechanism: Algorithmic order placement at mathematically determined levels creates self-fulfilling prophecy for technical levels
failure_modes: Algorithms detect and avoid crowded levels

title: Every bar conveys institutional intent information
claim: Each individual bar on a chart contains actionable information about institutional buying/selling pressure; no bar should be dismissed as unimportant or noise
support: Brooks emphasizes that traders must read charts bar-by-bar and extract information from every tick. Bar charting methodology stable over time.
mechanism: Aggregated OHLC data in each bar reflects buying/selling balance during that period; patterns emerge when multiple bars examined sequentially
assumptions: OHLC data accurately represents market activity
validation: Validate pattern recognition algorithms against manual bar-by-bar analysis

title: Strong trends feature pullbacks bought by institutional money
claim: In strong uptrends, pullbacks (bars closing below prior bar low) are tactical consolidations where institutions accumulate, not reversals; trend continues after pullback
support: Brooks illustrates that weak traders get stopped out during pullbacks while strong traders buy them; market continues higher afterward. Behavior pattern may degrade with market structure changes.
mechanism: Institutional buyers use pullbacks as liquidity accumulation points; weak-hand stops trigger below prior bars, followed by strong continuation
assumptions: Stop placement at conventional technical levels
failure_modes: No institutional bid at expected levels
validation: Backtest pullback-buy rules on historical equities; measure win rate vs random

title: Risk/reward ratio must equal or exceed 1:1
claim: Most setups require a profit objective (reward) that equals or exceeds the protective stop distance (risk); trading unfavorable ratios is eliminated
support: Brooks identifies risk/reward ratio as a foundational trade selection criterion. Fundamental risk principle that remains relevant.
mechanism: Favorable reward-to-risk allows profitable trading even with <50% win rate
assumptions: Stop placement achievable at intended level
Profit targets reachable in reasonable time
validation: Backtest confirms that strategies with >=1:1 ratio outperform <1:1 on cumulative return basis

title: Spectrum from extreme trend to extreme trading range
claim: Markets exist on a spectrum ranging from pure strong trend to pure trading range; price action analysis must identify current position on spectrum and adapt rules accordingly
support: Chapter 1 establishes that every market exhibits characteristics measurable along trend-to-range axis. Spectrum concept stable, but specific regime characteristics may shift.
mechanism: Market regime varies by timeframe, instrument, and time period; detection requires bar pattern analysis
assumptions: Regime stable long enough to trade
validation: Classify historical price series into trend/range regimes; validate classification against ex-post returns

title: Doji bars signal indecision and potential reversal
claim: Doji bars (close near open, small body, large wicks) indicate buyer-seller balance and often precede reversals or consolidation

source.section: Trend Bars, Doji Bars, and Climaxes

support: Chapter 2 defines doji bar morphology and market psychology. Bar pattern recognition stable.
mechanism: Large wicks show rejection of extreme prices; close near open shows indecision between buyers and sellers
failure_modes: Doji followed by continuation in trend direction
validation: Backtest doji-as-reversal signal on historical data; compare vs control

title: Outside bars mark potential breakouts and reversals
claim: Outside bars (high above prior bar high, low below prior bar low) indicate strong volatility expansion and often precede directional breakouts
support: Chapter 7 comprehensive analysis of outside bar patterns and trading rules. Pattern detection affected by market microstructure changes.
mechanism: Outside bar represents failed support and resistance; trapped stop orders; volatility surge attracts directional traders
failure_modes: Outside bar followed by mean reversion
False breakout (outside bar high/low not held)
validation: Backtest outside bar breakout signals; validate profitability vs entry-at-bar-close baseline

title: Bar close determines intrabar victory in buyer/seller battle
claim: The close of a bar is the most important price level; it determines where the majority of institutional money ended the period and indicates directional bias for next bars

source.section: The Importance of the Close of the Bar

support: Chapter 8 emphasizes that bar close (vs high/low/open) drives next-bar momentum and trader perception. Close still important but market microstructure (pre-market, post-market) expanded.
mechanism: Close determines buyer/seller perceived victory; influences stops, limit orders, and next open sentiment
failure_modes: Algorithmic trading responds to intrabar price more than close
Gap open invalidates prior close significance
validation: Compare next-bar returns when closed above vs below key levels; measure predictive power

title: Signal bars precede reversals with specific characteristics
claim: Reversal signal bars exhibit specific morphology (small body, one or two small tails on reversal side) and indicate nearby reversal probability; best reversal signals have favorable risk/reward
support: Chapter 5 defines reversal signal bar taxonomy and entry/exit mechanics. Pattern recognition dependent on bar data integrity.
mechanism: Reversal signal bar morphology shows institutional trapped shorts/longs; next bar often breaks out of bar range in opposite direction
failure_modes: Signal bar followed by continued trend
validation: Backtest reversal signal bar rules; measure profitability vs random entry

title: Trend lines provide structural support and entry points
claim: Trend lines drawn from swing lows/highs serve as dynamically-updating support and resistance; traders enter near trend line with stops below (for longs) and profit targets above key horizontal levels
support: Part II introduces trend lines as key structural framework; Chapter 13 covers construction and reliability. Trend line concept stable; implementation may vary.
mechanism: Trend line acts as magnet for price; bounces create entry/exit reference points
assumptions: Trend line drawn correctly (2+ points, slope stable)
failure_modes: Trend line redrawn too often (hindsight bias)
validation: Backtest trend line breakouts; measure profitability vs grid approach

title: Trading ranges have measurable characteristics
claim: Pure trading ranges (non-trending periods) have identifiable characteristics: smaller range, multiple touches of top/bottom, close proximity of high/low over multiple bars
support: Chapter 15 distinguishes trading range characteristics from trending structures. Range dynamics stable, but breakout probability may shift.
mechanism: Institutional traders consolidate during ranges; price bounces between identifiable highs/lows
failure_modes: False breakout followed by new range
validation: Classify historical price series into range/trend; backtest range-bound strategies

title: Trend entry requires signal bar followed by entry bar breakout
claim: Entry into trend trades typically requires: (1) signal bar (reversal or other pattern), (2) entry bar that breaks above/below signal bar; stop placed beyond signal bar extreme, profit target set for >=1:1 reward/risk

source.section: Example of How to Trade a Trend

support: Chapter 18 provides detailed example of trend trade mechanics including entry sequence and stop/target placement. Entry rules may require adjustment for current market microstructure.
mechanism: Signal bar identifies decision point; entry bar confirms breakout direction; stop at extreme price where institutional weakness appears
assumptions: Breakout followed by continuation (not false breakout)
failure_modes: False breakout (entry bar fails to hold)
validation: Backtest exact entry/stop/target rules from example on historical data

title: Parallel trend channels predict pullback targets and breakouts
claim: Trend lines with parallel lines (channels) define pullback zones and breakout targets; when price approaches channel bounds, reversal or breakout likely
support: Chapter 14 covers channel line construction and predictive bounce mechanics
mechanism: Channel defines trading range width; price reverts to mean (upper/lower line) or breaks out
validation: Backtest channel mean reversion and breakout rules

title: Two-leg pullback patterns identify trend continuation opportunities
claim: Two-leg pullbacks (first leg down in uptrend, second leg down before continuation) have identifiable structure; entry after second leg often precedes strong continuation
support: Chapter 20 covers two-leg pullback structure and entry rules
mechanism: Two-leg structure shows institutional accumulation and weak-hand capitulation; continuation follows
assumptions: First and second leg depths follow distribution
Entry timing after second leg precise
validation: Backtest two-leg structure entry rules; measure profitability
